question: What fluid mainly fills the hollow chambers (ventricles) inside the brain?
explanation: Great job! The brain ventricles are special hollow spaces that continuously make and store cerebrospinal fluid to keep the brain cushioned and nourished. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h1)

question: How does cerebrospinal fluid protect the brain from injury?

options.A: By providing buoyancy that reduces the net weight of the brain
options.B: By locking the brain rigidly in place to prevent all movement
options.C: By generating electrical currents that power nerve conduction
options.D: By inflating the skull bones to create a larger cranial vault

explanation: You got it! Floating in this fluid makes the heavy brain feel much lighter, keeping delicate tissue safe from being crushed by its own weight against the skull. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h1)

question: Which part of the brain houses the front sections (anterior horns) of the lateral ventricles?
explanation: Spot on! The front part of the lateral ventricle reaches forward right into the frontal lobe of the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h2)

question: What delicate structure separates the right and left lateral ventricles from each other?
explanation: Well done! The septum pellucidum is a thin, thin wall that sits right down the middle, separating the two lateral ventricles. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h2)

question: Where is the third ventricle located?

options.A: Within the central canal of the lumbar spinal cord
options.B: Directly beneath the outer surface of the occipital lobe
options.C: Inside the core tissue of the cerebellum
options.D: Between the left and right halves of the thalamus

explanation: You're doing great! The third ventricle sits right in the middle, snuggled between the left and right sides of the thalamus. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h3)

question: Which brain structure forms the roof at the back of the fourth ventricle?
explanation: Correct! The fourth ventricle sits right in front of the cerebellum, which forms its lovely protective roof at the back. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h3)

question: What is another common name for the channels connecting the lateral ventricles to the third ventricle?
explanation: You got it! These little connecting channels are famously known as the foramina of Monro. Keep this handy for exams! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h4)

question: Why is the cerebral aqueduct considered a high-risk spot for fluid blockage?

options.A: It contains sharp bony ridges that can cut surrounding neural tissue
options.B: It generates most of the cellular waste found in the brain
options.C: It pumps blood backward into the arterial system during high stress
options.D: Its narrow diameter makes it very prone to complete blockage from swelling

explanation: Spot on! Because it is the slimmest passage in the brain's plumbing system, even a tiny bit of swelling can easily block the flow. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h4)

question: Which specialized structure inside the ventricles makes cerebrospinal fluid?
explanation: Brilliant! The choroid plexus is like a tiny, hardworking sponge network inside the ventricles that constantly produces fresh cerebrospinal fluid. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h5)

question: About how much total cerebrospinal fluid does the human body produce every 24 hours?
explanation: You got it! Our bodies continuously refresh our CSF, making about 500 milliliters every single day. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h5)

question: Through which openings does cerebrospinal fluid leave the fourth ventricle to flow around the outside of the brain?
explanation: Well done! The median and lateral apertures act like exit doors in the fourth ventricle, letting fluid flow out into the subarachnoid space. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h6)

question: Where does cerebrospinal fluid ultimately drain back into after circulating around the brain?

options.A: Dural venous sinuses via arachnoid granulations
options.B: Bone marrow cavities within the cranium
options.C: Lymphatic vessels inside the deep neck muscles
options.D: Digestive tract through the base of the skull

explanation: Spot on! Once the fluid finishes its cleansing tour around the brain, arachnoid granulations return it safely back into the venous blood. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h6)

question: What is the medical term for the condition caused by a dangerous buildup of cerebrospinal fluid in the brain?
explanation: You're doing amazing! 'Hydrocephalus' literally means 'water on the brain,' referring to trapped fluid swelling up the ventricles. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h7)

question: Why does fluid build up in the ventricles in a patient with obstructive hydrocephalus caused by a brain tumor?

options.A: A physical mass is blocking the normal outflow channels of the ventricular system
options.B: The arachnoid villi are working too efficiently and pulling out too much blood
options.C: The brain cells are suddenly manufacturing ten times more fluid than normal
options.D: The cranial bones are expanding too fast for the fluid to fill the space

explanation: Exactly right! When a tumor or mass physically blocks the narrow drainage paths, the fluid gets trapped upstream, causing pressure to rise. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h7)
